column1: # p348 — a THIRD identity class, which neither of this base's two identity instruments can see.
# `gate-identity` (p283, offline) asks: do two shelf rows name the same ADDRESS?
# `gate-identity-online` (p283, egress) asks: do two addresses resolve to the same HEAD?
# Neither asks: do two DIFFERENT repositories ship the same PAYLOAD?
# They do, and the specimen was found while grading this pass's own promotion candidates — two
# addresses that the scope instrument reported with the same licence family and overlapping file
# names.  The skill bodies are byte-identical:
#   anthropics/k12-teacher-skills          plugin/skills/k12-check-for-understanding/SKILL.md
#   learning-commons-org/agent-skills      skills/k12-check-for-understanding/SKILL.md
# read at HEAD over raw.githubusercontent.com, both sha256 152e3272fbd108fe…  Different owners,
# different repositories, different HEADs, different directory layouts, SAME CONTENT.  Both are
# Apache-2.0 at the root, so there is no licence conflict — the cost is a DENOMINATOR error: a
# shelf that offers both as distinct assets double-counts the supply, and a client told "there are
# two open K-12 teacher skill packs" has been told something false.
# learning-commons-org's README names the relationship without claiming derivation: it points to
# "a companion K-12 teacher skills repository from Anthropic" that "accompanies this work", and
# says each skill carries its own attribution in a NOTICE file.  So this is a published pair, not
# a silent copy — which is exactly why an identity instrument has to measure the payload: the
# relationship is discoverable in prose and invisible to both gates.
# The ALIAS pair below is the other half of the coverage finding, and it is the one a case fold
# cannot reach: ONE repository under two owner strings with no characters in common.
check
payload digest
